title: ABI-Aware Dependency Analysis and CI Cache Policy Check

questions.prompt: Which approach best applies abi-aware dependency analysis and ci cache policy?
options: Shrink and stabilise ABI/dependency edges, then cache accurately modelled work under explicit compatibility and trust policy.
questions.answer: Shrink and stabilise ABI/dependency edges, then cache accurately modelled work under explicit compatibility and trust policy.
questions.explanation: The correct approach preserves Gradle’s lazy model, explicit data flow, variant correctness, functional evidence and operability.

questions.prompt: A remote build cache eliminates the cost of unnecessary ABI changes.
questions.explanation: Automatically removing every dependency labelled unused can break reflection, generated code, runtime service loading or tooling that static analysis cannot observe.

questions.prompt: Why can implementation dependencies improve build performance?
questions.answer: They keep internal dependency types off consumer compile ABIs, reducing classpaths and downstream invalidation.
questions.explanation: The answer names the model property that makes the build behaviour predictable rather than relying on incidental script order.
